claims.explanation: Monastrol selectively kills cells that depend on KIF11/Eg5-driven spindle bipolarity and have an intact or responsive mitotic checkpoint, so sensitivity is driven by high KIF11 expression and by loss of p53-mediated arrest/apoptosis, while protective features include functional p53 and intact DNA-damage/checkpoint signaling. The pattern is also consistent with mitotic vulnerability being enhanced by oncogenic RAS/BRAF-driven proliferation and by loss of tumor suppressors such as PTEN, whereas lines with intact p53 and/or alternative survival pathways are less affected.

features.basis: target expression determines monastrol sensitivity
p53 loss permits mitotic arrest/apoptosis after Eg5 inhibition
oncogenic RAS-driven proliferation increases mitotic dependence
BRAF-driven proliferation increases mitotic dependence
PTEN loss enhances PI3K/AKT survival signaling and mitotic vulnerability
loss of p16/CDKN2A releases cell-cycle brakes
RB1 loss may allow bypass of mitotic arrest
ATM loss impairs checkpoint signaling and reduces mitotic arrest
homologous recombination defects may increase mitotic stress sensitivity
SWI/SNF loss may alter mitotic gene expression and reduce drug response
NF2 loss observed in sensitive mesothelioma and thyroid lines
Wnt/beta-catenin activation observed in sensitive gastric and colorectal lines
